state: For a first supported local development profile, each preview build receives a fresh real D1 and must demonstrate member and outsider behavior through the production Identity/login/session stack. The account tables start empty. Registration cannot complete without a mail sender, which this profile lacks. A verified private Unix control socket is available to the local owner, while preview access is a different bootstrap cookie. The needed actor matrix is two colleagues on one team, another team's member, one signed-in user with no team, and anonymous. Evaluate bootstrap choices for correct authorization evidence, secure handling of local credentials, operational simplicity, and repeatability after rebuilds.

seed_strategy.instructions: Recommend a first-profile approach and identify any condition that would change the recommendation.

criteria.private_seed: Seed actual Identity records and memberships on each fresh preview, generate new passwords, and reveal them only in an owner-only control response. Login and team selection in the browser remain unchanged.
criteria.mail_sink: Include a local mail delivery sink and exercise normal registration to establish the actor matrix. This broadens auth coverage but requires an extra service and orchestration on every reset.
criteria.auth_shortcut: Use preview access as proof of app membership and let the browser proceed without real login. This reduces work, but invalidates login and policy evidence.
criteria.explicit_env: Require supplied local credentials, then create corresponding real Identity records in D1. This can suit customized setups, but creates a larger prerequisite for a novice agent.
